label: after
question: Why did it fall so much along the way?
answer:
The backtest shows a very large but temporary drawdown: DOCN’s worst drop began on February 18, 2025 and ended on August 1, 2025. The portfolio fell from $1,747 to $963, a 44.9% decline and a $784 loss. That took the position below the $1,000 starting capital before the later recovery.

There was probably not one single cause:

- **The decline began before the Q4 earnings release.** DigitalOcean reported its Q4 results on February 25. The company reported solid revenue growth, but its 2025 outlook called for roughly 13% growth and included front-loaded investment spending. [DigitalOcean’s Q4 results and 2025 outlook](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024-Financial-Results/default.aspx) give the company’s own figures. Investors may have viewed that growth rate and spending plan as less compelling than the valuation or expectations implied by the share price.

- **Investors remained sensitive to customer retention and growth quality.** Coverage at the time pointed to concerns about retention and gross margins, even though the reported financial results were positive. That helps explain why a growth stock could sell off despite revenue and profit increases.

- **The May earnings reaction added pressure.** DigitalOcean’s Q1 revenue reached $211 million and beat expectations, but the stock still fell after the report. [Contemporaneous coverage of the Q1 results](https://siliconangle.com/2025/05/06/digitalocean-shares-drop-despite-strong-first-quarter/) said the likely issue was forward guidance, particularly the Q2 outlook being below some analyst expectations.

- **The broader market selloff amplified the move.** In early April, tariff announcements triggered a sharp retreat from risky technology assets.
